content.value_statement: Clojure changes are hard to verify when edits, REPL checks, and style rules are separated. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused workflow for Metabase Clojure development.
actual_capabilities: Prefers clojure-mcp tools such as clojure_eval and clojure_edit when available.
Guides a bottom-up REPL workflow for small functions and composed changes.
Shows how to load a namespace through the Metabase mage REPL fallback.
Provides docstring guidance focused on caller contracts and useful constraints.
Defines editing checks for readable Clojure, final newlines, alignment, and whitespace.
limitations: It is tailored to Metabase Clojure and ClojureScript development patterns.
It depends on project tooling such as clojure-mcp or ./bin/mage for verification.
It does not replace tests, review, or domain knowledge for production changes.
It references shared documentation outside the skill directory in the source tree.

use_cases.title: Implement a Clojure Feature
use_cases.description: Break a feature into small functions, test each one in the REPL, and then compose the final change.

use_cases.title: Refactor ClojureScript Safely
use_cases.description: Use structural editing and repeated evaluation to reduce syntax errors during a ClojureScript refactor.

use_cases.title: Improve Docstrings
use_cases.description: Move implementation details out of docstrings and keep caller-facing contracts clear.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning before editing Clojure code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a small Clojure change. Identify the smallest functions to build first and the REPL checks to run after each edit.

prompt_templates.title: Write and Verify a Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the REPL-driven workflow to add the requested Clojure function. Prefer clojure-mcp tools when available, then summarize the checks performed.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Namespace
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced refactoring across an existing namespace.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this namespace using structural Clojure editing. Keep behavior stable, verify readability after each change, and note any tests that should be added.

prompt_templates.title: Review Docstrings and Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changed Clojure code for docstring quality, caller-facing contracts, whitespace, and missing test coverage. Suggest precise fixes.

output_examples.input: Add a helper function to a Metabase Clojure namespace.
output: A short implementation plan that starts with the smallest helper.
A verification summary covering namespace loading and representative REPL inputs.
Follow-up test suggestions for the new behavior.

output_examples.input: Clean up a long docstring in existing Clojure code.
output: A revised docstring focused on caller expectations.
Implementation notes moved near the relevant code path.
A brief explanation of why the new wording is easier to maintain.

output_examples.input: Refactor ClojureScript code while preserving behavior.
output: A sequence of small edits using structural Clojure conventions.
Readability and whitespace checks after the edits.
A concise risk note for areas that still need human review.

best_practices: Use clojure-mcp evaluation and editing tools before shell-based fallbacks.
Build small functions first, then compose them after REPL verification.
Keep docstrings focused on caller contracts, inputs, returns, and constraints.
anti_patterns: Do not make broad Clojure changes without evaluating each layer as it is built.
Do not leave implementation history or obvious facts in docstrings.
Do not ignore readability checks, final newlines, alignment, or trailing whitespace.

faq.question: What projects is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for Metabase Clojure and ClojureScript code that uses REPL-driven development.

faq.question: Does it require clojure-mcp?
faq.answer: No. It prefers clojure-mcp when available and documents a mage REPL fallback.

faq.question: Can it write production code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides the workflow, but code still needs tests, review, and project context.

faq.question: Does it include style guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers functional style, docstrings, whitespace, aligned tables, and readability checks.

faq.question: How does it help with refactoring?
faq.answer: It encourages small structural edits, repeated REPL checks, and behavior-focused tests.

faq.question: What should users review before installation?
faq.answer: Users should review the parent-directory shared document references and any local command fallback behavior.
